title: Movement, Inventory and Vendor-Neutral Tracking Records

content.overview: This lesson teaches the stable data principles behind plant and material movement records without pretending that one seed-to-sale software platform is universal.

vocabulary.definition: Comparison of physical material with the corresponding controlled record to identify and resolve differences.
A record showing authorized transfer of identified material from one location or status to another.
A process taught by its required data and controls rather than by assuming one software platform.

sections.title: Record what actually moved
sections.body: A movement record should correspond to a real authorized physical movement and preserve the required identity, source, destination, quantity or count where applicable, time and responsible person or system.

sections.title: Do not force reconciliation
sections.body: When physical material differs from the record, the technician verifies within procedure and documents the discrepancy. The worker does not change a digital count merely to make the screen match the expected number. Platform-specific training remains an employer or jurisdiction responsibility.

workedExamples: A work order expects 48 plants but the physical count is 47; the mismatch is verified and escalated before the movement is finalized.
The technician can preserve identifiers, counts, source, destination and timestamps even when the employer changes software platforms.
commonMistakes: Editing a count solely to make a record balance.
Claiming proficiency in a specific tracking platform from a vendor-neutral course.
content.practicalApplication: Complete a mock room-to-room movement and reconcile a second movement containing a planted physical-versus-record discrepancy.
content.summary: Good tracking follows physical reality. Technicians record movements contemporaneously, preserve identity and quantity data, and escalate discrepancies honestly.

blocks.title: Teach the data relationship, not one software screen
blocks.body: Tracking platforms differ, but a reliable movement still requires the same underlying logic: the correct identified material actually moves from a known source to an authorized destination, with the required quantity or count, time, and responsible record. Platform-specific clicks belong to employer or jurisdiction training.

blocks.alt: Flowchart comparing physical verification with the controlled record. Matching evidence is documented as verified; a mismatch triggers recounting, identifier and recent-event checks, preservation of the discrepancy, and escalation rather than changing a value merely to force agreement.
blocks.caption: Reconciliation compares evidence. It does not make one side automatically correct.

blocks.title: Stable movement-record fields
rows: What exact plant, batch, lot, container, or material moved?
Prevents movement from being detached from genealogy
Where or from what status did it leave?
Where or into what status did it go?
Links physical location to the record
Who or what recorded or executed the event?

blocks.title: The work order says 48; the physical count is 47
blocks.setting: A movement order expects 48 identified plants. You count 47. The software also shows 48 at the source location. The receiving room is waiting.
blocks.prompt: What is the strongest Technician I response?
options: Change the system to 47 so it matches the physical count
Add one to the physical count because the system is controlled
Verify the count and identifiers within procedure, preserve the discrepancy, and escalate if it cannot be reconciled before finalizing the movement
Move the 47 and close the order as 48
blocks.answer: Verify the count and identifiers within procedure, preserve the discrepancy, and escalate if it cannot be reconciled before finalizing the movement.
blocks.feedback: The physical state and the record are both evidence. The technician should not force either one to match the expected number without a controlled basis for the correction.

blocks.title: Inventory discrepancy handoff
blocks.description: Record enough context for the authorized reviewer to understand what was compared and what remains unresolved.

fields.label: Material / location
fields.value: Exact controlled identity and physical location

fields.label: Observed physical state
fields.value: Verified count, identity, location, or condition

fields.label: Checks performed
fields.value: Recount, identifier verification, permitted recent-event review

fields.label: Confirmed recent events
fields.value: Known movements, delayed entries, or transfers relevant to the mismatch

fields.label: Unresolved difference
fields.value: What still does not reconcile after permitted checks

fields.label: Immediate status
fields.value: Movement completed, paused, held, or otherwise controlled under procedure

fields.label: Escalation
fields.value: Role notified and next authorized action

blocks.title: Reconcile two mock movements
blocks.instructions: Complete one normal room-to-room movement and one movement containing a physical-versus-record discrepancy without relying on any named seed-to-sale platform.
prompts: Verify source and destination identities before movement.
Record the stable movement fields for the normal case.
Compare physical and recorded state in the discrepancy case.
List plausible causes without declaring an unsupported root cause.
Write the escalation packet without altering either value merely to make the record balance.

blocks.title: Key takeaway
blocks.body: Good tracking follows physical reality and preserves uncertainty when the evidence disagrees. Record the real movement, reconcile deliberately, and escalate unresolved differences without pretending one software platform defines the profession.
